_comment: Card Q3 SS2.1 -- 3 h GAUGE-FREE arm.  ONE knob different from
_golden63_3h_cta_on.json: network.clock_anchor_gauge_free.  Third arm of the
G3 ladder (ctl / anchor / anchor+gauge-free), same build, same config chain,
fresh convergence, runs never overlapping.
WHAT IT FIXES (measured, not theoretical).  The raw-state anchor puts prior
information on the per-constellation clock COMMON MODE, which is a GAUGE fixed
by the S-basis pivot pin, not by the carry.  Measured over the 3 h pair: the
anchored arm cut CLK-R's drained common mode Sigma|mu| 49.43 -> 27.77 m and the
pivot's dev row (which IS that drained common mode -- SPEC SS4.1) 16.79 -> 10.03
cm.  The carry was doing ~44 % of the datum's work.  This arm marginalizes the
gauge direction out of the folded information (rank-1 downdate
Lambda <- Lambda - Lambda u (u' Lambda u)^-1 u' Lambda), applied to the JOINT
dense block so the clock<->code-bias off-diagonals the C1 carry retains survive.
PRE-REGISTERED, AND THE SIGN IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE OBVIOUS GUESS:
* Sigma|mu| and the PIVOT dev row must RISE toward the control (49 m / 16.8
cm).  That is the mechanism working -- the gauge goes back to the data --
and it is harmless on the wire because CLK-R's frame hold drains that
channel at emission by construction.  A FALL would mean the downdate is
inert (check cta_gf_keys > 0 before reading anything else).
* EX-PIVOT dev ceiling and floor: unchanged or BETTER vs the anchor arm.
* sigma0_code: flat or better (the prior no longer competes with the pin, so
the pivot's rows stop carrying the conflict).
* consumer (live WTZZ): unchanged or better; 0 withholds; trips resolve and
mark exactly as in the anchor arm.
FRESH lineage (fingerprinted: the fold lives on a different subspace); run alone.
